verdict.rationale: Gmail's own filters run autonomously in the background: rules match incoming messages on criteria like sender, subject or size and automatically add or remove labels or forward mail. Users can create these filters straight from search results. However, the documented actions are narrow rule-based routing. Push notifications and the API are developer building blocks rather than a user-facing automation feature, and the Gemini actions shown are on-demand prompts, not background agents. Missing for 10: AI-driven or agentic background automations, triggers and actions beyond labeling and forwarding, a user-configurable workflow or scheduling builder, and independent corroboration.
